text.tspan: How to read it — and what not to read into it
Writing “dog”, the model spreads its attention over “on” (
) and gives the input word “dog” only

. That looks wrong — but with only two training sentences, any pattern that tells the two inputs apart is enough to write the right answer, and this one does. Attention maps of models trained on millions of
sentences are sharper and often line up with meaning; this map is a faithful picture of a model that memorised two examples.
The same plotting code, now showing a trained model’s real attention instead of an untrained model’s near-flat one.
